items.title: CISA Adds Four Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
items.one_liner: CISA added four actively exploited vulnerabilities—affecting SAP, Cisco, VMware, and Apache—to its KEV catalog under mandatory remediation rules.
items.summary: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added four known exploited vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, emphasizing active exploitation risks. The additions include CVE-2025-42884 in SAP NetWeaver, CVE-2026-76466 in Cisco Expressway Series, CVE-2026-123890 in VMware vCenter, and CVE-2026-129448 in Apache Roller. Under Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04, Federal Civilian Executive Branch agencies are mandated to rapidly remediate these high-risk vulnerabilities on exposed assets, while CISA strongly encourages all external organizations to adopt risk-based prioritization.
key_facts: CVE-2025-42884: SAP NetWeaver data query logic vulnerability
CVE-2026-76466: Cisco Expressway Series hard-coded credentials vulnerability
CVE-2026-123890: VMware vCenter authentication bypass vulnerability
items.bottom_line: Federal agencies must promptly patch four newly cataloged vulnerabilities in SAP, Cisco, VMware, and Apache to comply with CISA binding operational directives.

items.title: Cisco Expressway Series Remote Code Execution Vulnerability
items.one_liner: A critical remote code execution flaw in Cisco Expressway Series requires immediate patching as it is actively exploited in the wild.
items.summary: A vulnerability in the database service feature of Cisco Expressway Series can allow unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary OS commands as root. The issue stems from the use of persistent cookies and insufficient client certificate validation during TLS clustering. Cisco has released software updates to address the issue and has no available workarounds. The vulnerability has been added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog.
items.bottom_line: Unpatched Cisco Expressway devices face root-level compromise via persistent cookie abuse and RPC commands.

items.title: CVE-2026-123633 Portfolio Status: Impact of NGINX Vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-123007) on Palo Alto Networks Products (Severity: CRITICAL)
items.one_liner: Palo Alto Networks products running specific PAN-OS versions with HTTP/2 enabled are vulnerable to critical NGINX RCE flaws.
items.summary: Palo Alto Networks assessed the impact of two critical NGINX vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, affecting its PAN-OS and Panorama products. CVE-2026-123633 is a use-after-free issue in HTTP/2 proxy handling, while CVE-2026-123007 is an integer underflow leading to a heap-based buffer overflow. Both flaws allow unauthenticated remote attackers to execute arbitrary code or crash worker processes if HTTP/2 is enabled. Customers can mitigate the exposure by disabling HTTP/2 on PAN-OS and Panorama.
items.bottom_line: Disabling HTTP/2 on PAN-OS and Panorama provides an immediate workaround against critical NGINX RCE flaws.

items.title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
items.one_liner: Shirudo combines OpenAI's Codex and eBPF to deploy hot-patched security shields on running Linux systems.
items.summary: OpenAI and Cisco have introduced Shirudo, an open-source runtime utilizing eBPF to protect Linux systems during the patch deployment cycle. Shirudo allows security teams to run temporary safeguards called shields that block exploit vectors without restarting services or taking them offline. In tests, a Codex-generated shield successfully blocked a Java4Shell exploit against Elasticsearch. The project features hardware-backed verification via a Trusted Platform Module and cryptographically signed deployments.
items.bottom_line: eBPF-based shields can intercept and block live exploitation paths before official patches are applied.

items.title: CrowdStrike agrees to buy Zscaler for $43.9 billion in network security expansion
items.one_liner: CrowdStrike is acquiring Zscaler for $43.9 billion to unite endpoint security and zero-trust network access for modern cloud architectures.
items.summary: CrowdStrike has agreed to acquire Zscaler in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $43.9 billion to merge endpoint protection with cloud network security. The acquisition combines CrowdStrike's device and cloud workload monitoring with Zscaler's zero-trust network access control, addressing security requirements as corporate systems and AI agents connect directly to cloud applications. CrowdStrike plans to integrate device telemetry with network connection logs and cross-sell both platforms to Zscaler's roughly 8,000 customers. Zscaler CEO Jay Chaudhry will continue leading the business and join CrowdStrike's board upon closing, which is expected in the second half of fiscal 2028 pending regulatory and shareholder approvals.

items.title: Cleverbridge admits attackers stole customers' credit card and CVV numbers. Yep, you read that right
items.one_liner: A software e-commerce platform breach exposed customer card numbers and forbidden CVV data, presenting significant fraud risks for enterprise software buyers.
items.summary: Software e-commerce platform Cleverbridge admitted that hackers stole customer credit card numbers, expiration dates, contact details, and CVV security codes during an unauthorized intrusion detected on November 4. The breach directly violates PCI DSS rules, which strictly prohibit retaining CVV codes after authorization. The company serves enterprise IT vendors such as Red Hat, SUSE, and Veeam, though it has not disclosed the exact count of impacted users or specific corporate clients affected. Cleverbridge has notified data protection authorities, engaged a cybercrime police unit, and is offering affected customers 24 months of free credit monitoring.
items.bottom_line: Cleverbridge suffered a data breach where attackers stole customer credit card numbers and prohibited CVV codes, necessitating immediate card replacements for victims.

items.title: Linux kernel RCE CVE-2026-98432
items.one_liner: A Linux kernel use-after-free in IPv4 option handling permits potential RCE scenarios, requiring kernel updates or virtual patching.
items.summary: A use-after-free vulnerability, CVE-2026-98432, exists in the Linux kernel's IPv4 implementation where inet_opt and ireq_opt are freed after an RCU grace period. The flaw occurs because tcp_v4_syn_recv_sock() transfers ownership of ireq_opt without copying, leading to concurrency issues during retransmitted SYN processing and request socket migration. Fortinet confirmed that a virtual patch is available in FMWP database update 26.113 while many of its products remain unaffected.
items.bottom_line: Fixing Linux kernel socket option lifetime management prevents concurrent RCU-based use-after-free conditions.

items.one_liner: A reported breach of the FBI's National Crime Information Center database threatens millions of sensitive law enforcement and criminal history records.
items.summary: The FBI is investigating a reported breach of the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), a critical law enforcement database holding over 19.3 million records in fiscal year 2025. This intrusion represents the second reported security incident involving FBI systems in approximately two months, raising severe risks of targeted scams, extortion, and doxxing.

items.title: Microsoft Entra Connect Health Breach Exposes Tenant Metadata and Admin Details
items.one_liner: An API vulnerability in Microsoft Entra Connect Health exposed administrator contact details and tenant metadata, enabling targeted phishing risks.
items.summary: Microsoft disclosed a data breach affecting its Microsoft Entra Connect Health service, stemming from an API vulnerability introduced on July 23, 2026. Detected on November 9 and patched server-side on November 19, the flaw allowed unauthorized read-only access to tenant and service-monitoring metadata. While Microsoft confirmed that no passwords, authentication tokens, or cryptographic keys were compromised, the exposed data included administrator email addresses, tenant IDs, domain names, and synchronization statuses. This exposure creates severe risks for targeted phishing and social engineering attacks against administrators, prompting Microsoft to recommend security audits and phishing-resistant multi-factor authentication.

items.bottom_line: Unauthenticated read-only access to Entra Connect Health metadata has exposed administrator details, requiring organizations to audit logs and verify MFA.

items.title: Hackers leak data linked to Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan customers
items.one_liner: Third-party vendor breaches exposed non-financial customer data for major card networks, providing scammers with material for targeted phishing.
items.summary: A ransomware and extortion group named n0n leaked data belonging to customers of major financial institutions, including Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan Chase, following security incidents at third-party vendors. The affected companies confirmed that their core payment processing networks were untouched and no payment card numbers were exposed. However, the leaked files included marketing data, names, email addresses, phone numbers, and dining or travel bookings originating from third-party partners handling loyalty and benefit programs. Security researchers noted that the exposed non-financial data could be exploited by scammers to execute highly convincing phishing attacks.

items.title: Agents didn’t break code review, they exposed it
items.one_liner: AI coding agents are flooding codebases with volume, forcing software teams to confront the breakdown of traditional human code review.
items.summary: Software development veteran John Crickett explains how the surge in code volume produced by AI coding agents has exposed existing weaknesses in traditional human code review processes. Under intense delivery pressure, developers are increasingly skipping thorough reviews or losing the ability to understand large blocks of generated code. Crickett points out that human code review of massive pull requests was already unreliable and largely symbolic. While AI-based code review models provide fast and repeatable checks, teams remain entirely accountable for verifying the production readiness and security of all shipped code.
items.bottom_line: The massive volume of code generated by AI agents has broken traditional human review safeguards, requiring teams to update their verification practices.

claims.text: AI agents have changed code review primarily by exponentially increasing the volume of code.
claims.support_span: What agents have really changed is the volume of code. It now arrives faster than anyone can read it, and the traditional safeguard of a reviewer approving each diff was never as dependable as teams assumed.

claims.text: Large 500-line code changes historically received quick approvals because humans cannot hold complex changes in their heads.
claims.support_span: a reviewer easily scrutinizes five lines, finds 50 lines a bit harder, but a 500-line change “just gets a LGTM. Because most people cannot hold in their head five hundred lines of complex code change.”

items.title: Signal Is Blocking AI Agents From Reading Your Screen
items.one_liner: Signal is actively blocking OS-level AI agents from reading its interface to maintain its privacy guarantees against screen-scraping AI.
items.summary: Signal is implementing technical blocks to prevent OS-level AI agents, such as Google's Gemini and Apple's Siri AI, from reading its application screen on iOS and Android. The company argues that these AI agents undermine its privacy guarantees by capturing and processing screen content, which may be stored or transmitted outside of Signal's control. While Signal has blocked screenshots on iOS and screen capture on Android, it notes that this does not prevent agents from accessing data via the filesystem. Signal is calling on major OS providers to offer developers clear, granular controls to opt-out of AI agent data access.
key_facts: Targeted AI: Google Gemini, Apple Siri AI
items.bottom_line: Signal's move to block AI screen-scraping highlights the growing conflict between OS-integrated AI agents and application-level privacy models.

items.title: VirtualBox Process Hardening on Windows 2026 Edition: What’s a Single Bit Between Friends?
items.one_liner: A new VirtualBox vulnerability (CVE-2026-87268) allows arbitrary code execution by abusing .NET memory-based assembly loading to bypass process hardening.
items.summary: Google Project Zero researcher identified new bypasses for Oracle VirtualBox's process hardening on Windows, specifically focusing on CVE-2026-87268. The vulnerability exploits the .NET Framework's ability to load assemblies from memory buffers, which bypasses DLL loader hooks used by VirtualBox to verify loaded modules. By leveraging this behavior, an attacker can load arbitrary code into a protected process. This research highlights the risks of relying on standard runtime features to enforce process security.
items.bottom_line: VirtualBox's process hardening can be bypassed by abusing .NET Framework features to load unsigned code, rendering existing DLL verification checks ineffective.

items.one_liner: Git 2.56.1 and backports fix six critical security flaws, including code execution during cloning and path traversal.
items.summary: The Git project has released security patches across multiple maintenance series, culminating in Git 2.56.1, to address six vulnerabilities including arbitrary code execution, path traversal, and stack corruption. CVE-2026-111760 involves an integer truncation vulnerability during index handling that permits an attacker-controlled Git server to overwrite repository metadata or execute code during cloning. Other fixed issues include path traversal via protocol v2 HEAD advertisements (CVE-2026-113408), stack corruption from excessive GPG signatures during merges (CVE-2026-114467), and out-of-bounds reads when applying compressed binary patches. Administrators and developers should update Git installations and dependent applications immediately.

items.one_liner: CVE-2026-124283 allows unauthenticated RCE and SQL injection via forged keyset pagination cursors in the Ash framework.
items.summary: A deserialization vulnerability designated as CVE-2026-124283 affects the ash-project ash framework from version 3.31.3 before 3.38.0. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code or inject SQL via a forged keyset pagination cursor supplied in Erlang external term format. The vulnerability stems from the framework's failure to examine struct fields within decoded sort expressions, permitting chosen struct modules to reach the data layer and invoke command execution functions. When used with AshPostgres, passing a crafted struct to inspect/1 leads to OS command execution and raw text SQL injection. Remotely exploiting the issue allows attackers to leverage selected struct modules to execute commands.

Researchers demonstrated reading approximately 127 GB of host RAM and writing chosen bytes into live host kernel memory. The issue stems from KVM failing to restore an outer virtual CPU pointer when an INIT reset signal stops a nested virtual machine, leaving it pointing to freed memory. Upstream Linux kernel maintainers merged a fix, and affected cloud providers and operators must update host kernels or disable nested virtualization. The Linux kernel CVE team rates the flaw 8.8, whereas Red Hat rates it 5.6 as a denial-of-service issue.
key_facts: Memory exposed: ~127 GB of host RAM
Affected hardware: AMD processors with nested virtualization enabled
items.bottom_line: CVE-2026-99312 permits guest VMs to access up to 127 GB of host RAM on AMD KVM hosts with nested virtualization enabled, requiring an immediate kernel update.

items.bottom_line: Defenders must audit application permissions and identity relationships across cloud and on-premises environments before automated threat agents exploit hidden attack paths.

items.title: We caught the agent-framework PyPI compromise six minutes after it published
items.one_liner: Elastic Security Labs detailed how malicious agent-framework PyPI versions automatically executed credential-stealing hooks upon Python startup.
items.summary: Compromised versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of Microsoft's agent-framework PyPI meta-package shipped with a malicious .pth startup script designed to harvest credentials whenever Python runs on an affected host. Discovered by Elastic Security Labs shortly after publication, the payload executes automatically on interpreter startup without requiring package import, extracting environment variables, token caches, and container registry credentials from running processes. The stealer then pings Azure DevOps and GitHub Actions OIDC endpoints alongside IMDS to generate fresh cloud access tokens, exfiltrating all compressed data to a webhook endpoint.
items.bottom_line: The inclusion of a .pth execution hook in compromised agent-framework packages ensures that credential theft occurs automatically upon any Python process start on infected machines.

items.summary: OpenAI and Cisco have released 'Shirudo', an open-source tool built on eBPF designed to place temporary security protections on running Linux systems while patches are developed and tested. Shirudo blocks specific vulnerability-dependent behaviors without requiring service restarts, allowing defenders to verify that blocks prevent attacks while maintaining normal traffic flow. The tool enforces cryptographic signature verification and logs protection events to a Trusted Platform Module (TPM) 2.0 chip, though production deployment requires kernel patches and a TPM 2.0 device.
key_facts: Requirements: Linux kernel with Shirudo patches and a TPM 2.0 chip
Components: eBPF programs, cryptographically signed shields
items.bottom_line: Defenders can use Shirudo's eBPF-based temporary shields to block active exploits on running Linux systems while official patches are being prepared.

items.title: Ransomware Recovery Takes 20 Days for the Typical Victim, Report Finds
items.one_liner: Ransomware recovery is a prolonged process averaging 20 days, with attackers actively targeting backup infrastructure to prevent restoration.
items.summary: A report by Rubrik Zero Labs indicates that the median time for ransomware recovery is 20 days, with nearly 30% of victims requiring more than six weeks to return to normal operations. The study, based on 16,953 incidents in 2026, highlights that attackers are increasingly targeting backup environments to hinder restoration efforts. Data theft is now a more common extortion tactic than encryption, appearing in 67% of cases compared to 45% for encryption. The threat landscape remains concentrated, with just eight groups responsible for approximately half of all attributed attacks.
items.bottom_line: Organizations must prioritize the security of their backup management consoles, as attackers are increasingly targeting these systems to ensure extortion success.

items.title: AI Coding Agents Are Getting Malicious Results From Web Search Indexes, WebSec Benchmark Finds
items.one_liner: AI coding agents blindly execute malicious payloads from web search results, with all major search APIs serving known-bad content in benchmark tests.
items.summary: AI coding agents frequently execute malicious content encountered during web searches because they lack human skepticism, leading to automated compromise when evaluating top search results. AIR Research Lab's WebSec Benchmark testing across eight search APIs found that every provider served known-malicious content at rates between 0.8% and 2.2% of searches, with package installation and error resolution queries posing the highest risks. Attackers exploit this behavior by publishing high-ranking malicious repositories—such as the SolanaCry malware deployed via PowerShell—or by registering lapsed domains that still appear in developer search queries. This creates an immediate attack vector where autonomous tools execute remote access tools and steal crypto wallets without any user interaction.
key_facts: Search APIs tested: Firecrawl, Tavily, Perplexity, Parallel, Exa, Nimble, Brave, You.com
Malicious content rate: 0.8% to 2.2% per API
items.bottom_line: AI coding agents automatically execute malicious instructions found in search results, turning routine web queries into remote code execution risks.

items.title: Bangladesh's ex-PM Sheikh Hasina says she plans to return on 16 December
items.one_liner: Ousted former Bangladeshi PM Sheikh Hasina plans to return from exile on Victory Day, triggering sharp pushback from Dhaka over outstanding criminal sentences.
items.summary: Bangladesh's ousted former prime minister Sheikh Hasina announced plans to return to Dhaka on December 16, coinciding with the country's Victory Day, over two years after fleeing to India following mass uprisings. Her spokesperson stated that Hasina has asked the Bangladeshi government to arrange air transport from Delhi, while her party, the Awami League, continues street protests despite being banned. Bangladeshi state minister for foreign affairs Humayun Kabir dismissed her return on commercial terms, stating she would be brought back in handcuffs to face justice. Hasina was previously sentenced to death in absentia by a Bangladeshi court for crimes against humanity related to the deadly crackdown on student-led protests that ended her 15-year rule. The diplomatic tensions over her potential extradition and return add to ongoing political instability following the rise of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman's government.

items.title: CVE-2026-135736 - FFmpeg 4.4 before 9.1 Heap Out-of-Bounds Write via deband Filter Coupling Command
items.one_liner: CVE-2026-135736 is a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in FFmpeg's deband filter that can cause crashes or code execution.
items.summary: FFmpeg versions 4.4 before 9.1 contain a heap out-of-bounds read and write vulnerability in libavfilter/vf_deband.c. Attackers can trigger the vulnerability by sending a runtime coupling command, such as 'deband coupling 1', via sendcmd or an unauthenticated zmq filter. This forces chroma planes to be processed at luma dimensions, resulting in process crashes or potential code execution.
items.bottom_line: FFmpeg instances below version 9.1 must be updated to prevent memory corruption and potential code execution via malformed deband commands.

items.summary: Iranian singer Parastoo Ahmadi and four male co-defendants were given 74 lashes each at an enforcement office in Qom after being convicted of offending public decency by performing without a hijab. items.title: The Vulnerability Playbook Is Broken: A CISO’s Cheat Sheet To AI-Era Cybersecurity
items.one_liner: JFrog argues that AI-driven exploitation requires transitioning from manual vulnerability patching to a five-layer self-healing software supply chain.
items.summary: JFrog Security outlines how the traditional vulnerability remediation playbook has broken down in the AI era due to frontier models discovering zero-days and generating working exploits before disclosures or patches exist. Because the time window between flaw existence and active exploitation has collapsed to near zero, manual triage and sequential PR reviews fail to match machine speed. The report argues that organizations cannot rely solely on upstream vendor fixes or human approval gates, especially when running self-hosted environments. To survive machine-speed threats, companies must adopt a five-layer, self-healing software supply chain architecture that automates prevention, detection, and remediation across development pipelines.
items.bottom_line: Traditional vulnerability remediation is obsolete because frontier AI models enable exploitation before fixes are published, forcing organizations to adopt automated self-healing supply chain architectures.

items.summary: Bishop Fox published an AI security assessment framework arguing that shallow automated scans miss critical risks where AI model outputs turn into database queries, API calls, and agent actions. The standard advocates for a full-stack, six-step approach combining adversarial AI testing with traditional web, API, cloud, and identity assessments to prove real blast radii. items.bottom_line: Securing AI deployments requires full-stack testing that evaluates how model outputs interface with underlying databases, APIs, and agent actions.

items.summary: Preemptive Managed Detection and Response (MDR) connects exposure context, threat intelligence, AI-assisted investigation, and human expertise to help security teams prioritize vulnerabilities before exploitation occurs. An attacker must also intercept or redirect the victim’s connection to exploit that trust.

items.title: The problem with shared Wi-Fi passwords at work
items.summary: TL;DR - WPA2-PSK gives everyone the same Wi-Fi password. If that password is exposed, anyone with it can access the network until the password is changed. Replace shared Wi-Fi password authentication type (WPA2-PSK) with better Wi‑Fi security protocol such as WPA2/3-Enterprise and use secure authentication methods such as certificate-based authentication to provide unique credentials for each user and device. Where WPA2-PSK is the only option, ensure strong passwords are used. Restrict WPA2-PSK networks to guest access only and ensure they are segregated from internal corporate systems.
